description:
FILED s492c (Opus, 2026-09-21) as the residue of #1870.

Member 1 routed the GENERIC funcall path and the readpipe/backtick path
through `Pl::Environment::builtin_override_target`, which took
t/op/override.t from 3 ok / 17 not-ok to 9/13 (six rows fixed, shortfall
16 -> 14).  The 28 rows still failing are three constructs that have their
own emission sites and never consult the registry:

  * `require` -- and it is the interesting one: perl calls the override with
    the FILENAME it computed, so `require Foo::Bar` passes "Foo/Bar.pm" and
    `require 5.006` passes "5.006".  PCL's `require BAREWORD` emission already
    computes the module path, so the fix is to emit
    `(|CORE::GLOBAL|::pl-require "Foo/Bar.pm")` there.  8 rows, plus the
    `local *CORE::GLOBAL::require` rows, which also need the override lookup
    to be a RUNTIME read of the glob rather than a compile-time constant.
  * `readline` / `<FH>` / `<$fh>` / rcatline -- 8 rows.
  * `do FILE` and the `sub CORE::GLOBAL::do;` forward-declaration stub form.

Also unrouted: `*{q|CORE::GLOBAL::readpipe|} = ...` (the BLOCK spelling of a
glob name, as opposed to the bareword `*CORE::GLOBAL::readpipe`), which
op/override.t uses inside `runperl` sub-programs.

The registry and its one reader are in place, so each of these is "call
`builtin_override_target` at this site and emit the qualified name", not a
new mechanism.
subject: `*CORE::GLOBAL::require` / `::do` / `::readline` are separate EMISSION SITES and are not routed through the override registry -- 28 of t/op/override.t`s rows
